pack.name: Survival manuals
pack.attribution: US Army ATP 3-50.21, ATP 4-02.11, TC 21-3, TC 3-97.61 and TC 3-21.60; FEMA Are You Ready?

_notes: Every url below was fetched on 2026-11-09 and returned 2xx with Content-Type application/pdf and a %PDF- magic header. armypubs.army.mil answered plain urllib with and without a User-Agent and honours HEAD, so no special client handling is needed.
The ATP 3-50.21 path contains literal spaces and they must stay percent-encoded as %20.

FEMA no longer hosts the 2004 ~204-page 'Are You Ready? IS-22' full PDF. Every fema.gov path for it 404s and IS-22 itself is retired (it redirects to IS-909). What is published is the current 36-page Ready.gov edition, listed below. The long 2004 edition survives only on non-federal mirrors, which are not used here: a survival manual served from an unverifiable mirror is exactly the thing this pipeline exists to avoid. OPEN QUESTION in the repo README.
ATP 4-25.13 is no longer in the active ATP index; ATP 4-02.11 (23 Mar 2026) supersedes TC 4-02.1 and is the current Army first-aid publication.

TC 3-25.26 Map Reading and Land Navigation (15 Nov 2013, ARN43276, supersedes FM 3-25.26) is skipped. It is still the active edition, but armypubs serves it from DR_c, which 302-redirects to the CAC login at federation.eams.army.mil, so the PDF cannot be fetched publicly and its distribution statement could not be read. (Copies on university ROTC sites are not used.)

MCRP 3-40.3B Radio Operator's Handbook (2 Jun 1999, formerly MCRP 6-22C) is skipped. It is no longer listed in the marines.mil MCPEL, and no renumbered successor was found there. The only official-host copy, www.trngcmd.marines.mil/Portals/207/Docs/TBS/MCRP%203-40.3B%20Radio%20Operators%20Handbook.pdf (2,154,049 bytes, 145 pages), has no distribution statement at all: its front matter is cut down to a cover and table of contents. With no public-release statement in the PDF, it does not qualify.

AFH 10-644 (SERE) was left out on purpose: static.e-publishing.af.mil returns 403 to scripted downloads, so the pipeline could not fetch or re-check it. Revisit if the Air Force host allows plain HTTP clients.
